outputs.L3:
Dermatopontin (DPT), or a functional fragment thereof, is provided for use in maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells in culture. In particular, DPT or a functional fragment thereof may be used to support the survival, maintenance, and/or preservation of hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells under in vitro culture conditions. The hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells may be maintained in an undifferentiated or substantially undifferentiated state, or in a state in which their stem and/or progenitor cell characteristics are at least partially retained.

The invention therefore provides a method of culturing hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells, the method comprising culturing the cells in the presence of DPT or a functional fragment thereof. The DPT or functional fragment may be added to the culture medium, immobilized on a culture surface, incorporated into a matrix or scaffold, or otherwise presented to the cells in a manner that promotes maintenance of the hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cell population. The method may be used for culturing cells obtained from bone marrow, peripheral blood, umbilical cord blood, fetal liver, mobilized blood, or other suitable hematopoietic sources.

In some embodiments, the hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells are cultured under conditions suitable for maintaining cell viability, supporting limited expansion, preserving multipotency, reducing differentiation, or maintaining the capacity of the cells to engraft or reconstitute hematopoiesis. The concentration and form of DPT or the functional fragment thereof may be selected according to the cell type, culture conditions, and intended use of the cultured cells.

The invention further provides a cell culture medium for maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells, wherein the medium comprises DPT or a functional fragment thereof. The culture medium may be a basal medium suitable for hematopoietic cell culture and may further comprise one or more additional components that support cell survival or maintenance. Such components may include, for example, serum, a serum replacement, one or more reducing agents, and/or one or more antibiotics.

In certain embodiments, the serum may be fetal bovine serum, human serum, or another suitable animal-derived or human-derived serum. Alternatively, the medium may be serum-free and may comprise a defined serum replacement. Suitable reducing agents may include, but are not limited to, β-mercaptoethanol, dithiothreitol, glutathione, or other agents capable of maintaining a suitable redox environment. Suitable antibiotics may include penicillin, streptomycin, amphotericin B, gentamicin, or other antimicrobial agents commonly used in cell culture. The medium may also include cytokines, growth factors, nutrients, buffers, amino acids, vitamins, salts, or other supplements suitable for hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cell culture.

The invention also provides a kit for use in culturing or maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells. The kit comprises DPT or a functional fragment thereof and may further comprise one or more components selected from a culture medium, cytokines, growth factors, serum, serum replacement, reducing agents, antibiotics, buffers, supplements, culture vessels, matrices, coatings, or instructions for use. The DPT or functional fragment may be supplied in liquid, lyophilized, frozen, concentrated, or ready-to-use form. Where appropriate, the components of the kit may be supplied separately or in combination.

The kit may be used to prepare a culture system for maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells in vitro. For example, the kit may include DPT or a functional fragment thereof together with a basal medium and one or more cytokines suitable for hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cell culture. The kit may optionally include serum or a serum replacement, a reducing agent, and an antibiotic formulation. Instructions may be provided for reconstituting, diluting, combining, or applying the components in order to culture hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells under conditions that support their maintenance.
outputs.L4:
The present invention relates to the ex vivo maintenance, preservation, and culture of hematopoietic stem cells and/or hematopoietic progenitor cells. More particularly, the invention is based on the finding that dermatopontin (DPT), or a functional fragment, variant, or derivative thereof, can be used as an effective component in culture systems designed to maintain hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells outside the body. By incorporating DPT into a culture medium, coating, matrix, supplement, or cell culture kit, the invention provides improved methods for preserving the desirable properties of these cells during ex vivo handling.

Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are valuable for a wide range of clinical, research, and biotechnological applications, including transplantation, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, disease modeling, and drug screening. However, maintaining these cells in culture can be difficult, because they may lose stemness, differentiate prematurely, decline in viability, or exhibit reduced engraftment potential over time. Conventional culture systems often require combinations of cytokines, growth factors, serum components, feeder cells, or extracellular matrix materials, but these approaches may not adequately preserve the most primitive and therapeutically useful cell populations.

The invention identifies dermatopontin as a useful factor for supporting hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells in vitro or ex vivo. DPT may be provided as a purified or recombinant protein, as a biologically active fragment, or as a component immobilized on a culture surface, incorporated into a scaffold, or dissolved or suspended in a liquid culture medium. The DPT or functional fragment thereof may be used alone or in combination with other culture components, including basal media, serum or serum replacements, cytokines, chemokines, extracellular matrix proteins, small molecules, nutrients, antibiotics, or other supplements that support hematopoietic cell survival and function.

In one aspect, the invention provides a method for maintaining hematopoietic stem cells and/or hematopoietic progenitor cells in culture, the method comprising contacting the cells with DPT or a functional fragment thereof under conditions suitable for cell survival. The cells may be obtained from bone marrow, peripheral blood, mobilized peripheral blood, umbilical cord blood, fetal liver, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic populations, embryonic stem cell-derived hematopoietic populations, or any other suitable source. The method may be used to maintain cell viability, preserve an undifferentiated or less differentiated phenotype, retain colony-forming capacity, support self-renewal-associated characteristics, or improve functional properties relevant to transplantation or further manipulation.

In another aspect, the invention provides a culture medium comprising DPT or a functional fragment thereof for use in culturing hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells. The medium may be formulated as a ready-to-use liquid medium, a concentrated supplement, a lyophilized preparation for reconstitution, or a defined or semi-defined medium component. The medium may be serum-free, xeno-free, feeder-free, or otherwise adapted for clinical-grade cell processing. The presence of DPT in the medium may improve the ability of the culture system to maintain hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells during expansion, storage, genetic modification, differentiation control, or preparation for administration to a subject.

In a further aspect, the invention provides a kit for culturing or maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells. The kit may comprise DPT or a functional fragment thereof, optionally together with one or more additional reagents such as a basal culture medium, cytokines, buffers, culture vessels, coated plates, matrices, instructions for use, or reagents for evaluating cell phenotype or function. The kit may be configured for laboratory research, clinical cell processing, transplantation preparation, gene-editing workflows, or other applications involving hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.

The invention therefore provides a practical approach for improving ex vivo hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell culture. By using dermatopontin as a defined culture component, the invention supports the development of more reliable and effective culture systems for maintaining these clinically and scientifically important cells. Such systems may reduce loss of stem or progenitor cell function during culture, improve consistency between preparations, and facilitate downstream applications requiring viable and functionally competent hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style summary for an invention involving dermatopontin (DPT) or functional fragments for maintaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in culture, including medium and kit embodiments.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent-Style Summary

The present disclosure relates generally to compositions and methods for maintaining hematopoietic stem and/or progenitor cells in vitro, and more particularly to the use of dermatopontin (DPT), or functional fragments, variants, derivatives, or mimetics thereof, to preserve, maintain, expand, or enhance hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell properties during culture.

In one aspect, the disclosure provides a cell culture medium comprising a basal hematopoietic cell culture medium and an effective amount of dermatopontin (DPT) or a functional fragment thereof. In certain embodiments, the DPT is a mammalian DPT, including human DPT, recombinant DPT, purified DPT, synthetic DPT, or a biologically active fragment or variant retaining the ability to support hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell maintenance. In some embodiments, the medium further comprises one or more hematopoietic growth factors, cytokines, extracellular matrix components, small molecules, serum substitutes, albumin, lipids, nutrients, or combinations thereof. Exemplary additional agents include stem cell factor (SCF), thrombopoietin (TPO), Flt3 ligand, interleukins, angiopoietin-like proteins, insulin-transferrin-selenium supplements, or other agents suitable for culturing hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.

In another aspect, the disclosure provides a method of maintaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in culture, comprising contacting a population of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells with DPT or a functional fragment thereof under culture conditions sufficient to maintain one or more stem or progenitor cell characteristics. In certain embodiments, the method maintains, preserves, increases, or enriches cells having hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell activity, including cells expressing one or more markers selected from CD34, CD38, CD90, CD45RA, CD49f, CD133, c-Kit, Sca-1, lineage-negative markers, or combinations thereof, depending on species. In particular embodiments, the cultured cells retain multilineage differentiation potential, colony-forming capacity, engraftment potential, self-renewal potential, quiescence, viability, or reduced differentiation relative to cells cultured in the absence of DPT.

In some embodiments, the hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells are obtained from bone marrow, mobilized peripheral blood, umbilical cord blood, fetal liver, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic cultures, embryonic stem cell-derived hematopoietic cultures, or genetically modified hematopoietic cells. In certain embodiments, the cells are human CD34-positive cells. In other embodiments, the cells are murine lineage-negative, Sca-1-positive, c-Kit-positive cells, or other hematopoietic stem/progenitor populations.

In certain embodiments, DPT or the functional fragment thereof is provided in soluble form in the medium. In other embodiments, DPT or the functional fragment thereof is immobilized on a culture surface, bead, scaffold, hydrogel, extracellular matrix substrate, nanoparticle, or other support. In further embodiments, DPT is provided as part of a coating for a cell culture vessel or as a component of a three-dimensional culture matrix. The DPT may be used alone or in combination with additional niche-associated molecules, including collagen, fibronectin, laminin, vitronectin, tenascin, osteopontin, heparan sulfate proteoglycans, or fragments thereof.

In another aspect, the disclosure provides a method of expanding or preserving transplantable hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells ex vivo, comprising culturing hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in a medium comprising DPT or a functional fragment thereof for a period sufficient to obtain a cultured cell population having maintained or enhanced hematopoietic repopulating activity. In some embodiments, the cultured cells are subsequently administered to a subject in need of hematopoietic reconstitution, immune reconstitution, gene therapy, cell therapy, or treatment of a hematologic disorder. In certain embodiments, the cells are genetically modified before, during, or after culture in the presence of DPT.

In another aspect, the disclosure provides a composition comprising hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and DPT or a functional fragment thereof. In certain embodiments, the composition is a culture composition, cryopreservation composition, transplantation composition, or intermediate manufacturing composition. In some embodiments, the composition comprises human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells cultured in the presence of DPT and retaining improved engraftment, viability, or stemness compared with a corresponding composition cultured without DPT.

In another aspect, the disclosure provides a kit for maintaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in culture. The kit may comprise DPT or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, or mimetic thereof, and instructions for use in culturing hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells. In certain embodiments, the kit further comprises one or more of a basal medium, cytokine supplement, serum-free supplement, culture vessel, DPT-coated culture substrate, extracellular matrix component, buffer, cell selection reagent, cryopreservation reagent, or written protocol. In particular embodiments, the kit comprises a sterile container containing recombinant human DPT and instructions for adding the DPT to a hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell culture medium at an effective concentration.

In further embodiments, the disclosure provides a coated article of manufacture comprising a cell culture surface having immobilized thereon DPT or a functional fragment thereof. The coated article may be a culture flask, plate, bag, microcarrier, bead, fiber, membrane, scaffold, microfluidic device, or bioreactor component. In some embodiments, the coated article is used to maintain hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in an undifferentiated or less differentiated state during ex vivo culture.

Functional fragments of DPT useful in the disclosed methods and compositions include fragments that retain the capacity to maintain hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell viability, phenotype, quiescence, self-renewal, colony-forming activity, or engraftment activity. In certain embodiments, the fragment comprises one or more domains, motifs, or amino acid sequences of DPT sufficient to bind a cellular receptor, extracellular matrix component, integrin-associated pathway component, or other molecule involved in hematopoietic niche signaling. Variants may include amino acid substitutions, deletions, additions, fusion proteins, pegylated forms, glycosylation variants, tagged proteins, or other modified forms retaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell-supporting activity.

In certain embodiments, an effective amount of DPT or functional fragment is an amount sufficient to produce a measurable improvement in one or more hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell parameters compared with culture in a corresponding medium lacking DPT. Such parameters may include increased frequency or absolute number of phenotypic stem/progenitor cells, increased colony-forming units, increased long-term culture-initiating cells, increased serial replating capacity, increased engraftment in an immunodeficient recipient, increased multilineage reconstitution, reduced apoptosis, reduced differentiation, altered cell cycle status, or improved recovery after cryopreservation.

The disclosure further encompasses use of DPT or a functional fragment thereof in the manufacture of a medium, reagent, coated substrate, or kit for maintaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells in culture, as well as the use of DPT or a functional fragment thereof to improve ex vivo manufacturing of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell products.

Below is example broad patent-style language covering use of dermatopontin (“DPT”) or functional fragments thereof in ex vivo culture of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (“HSPCs”). This language is illustrative and should be adapted to the specific experimental support and jurisdiction.

---

## Exemplary Claim Language

### 1. Method Claims

1. **A method of expanding, maintaining, enriching, or preserving hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells ex vivo,** the method comprising culturing a population of cells comprising hematopoietic stem cells, hematopoietic progenitor cells, or both, in a culture medium comprising dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof, under conditions sufficient to expand, maintain, enrich, or preserve the hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the dermatopontin comprises mammalian dermatopontin.

3. The method of claim 1 or 2, wherein the dermatopontin comprises human dermatopontin.

4. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the dermatopontin comprises a recombinant dermatopontin polypeptide.

5. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the functional fragment comprises a portion of dermatopontin that retains activity in supporting ex vivo survival, proliferation, self-renewal, engraftment potential, adhesion, maintenance, or expansion of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.

6. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is soluble in the culture medium.

7. The method of any of claims 1-5, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is immobilized on a culture surface, substrate, particle, hydrogel, scaffold, membrane, bead, nanoparticle, or extracellular matrix material.

8. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is present in the culture medium at a concentration effective to increase the number, frequency, viability, colony-forming capacity, engraftment capacity, or stemness of the hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells relative to a comparable culture lacking the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof.

9. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the population of cells is obtained from cord blood, mobilized peripheral blood, bone marrow, fetal liver, placental blood, peripheral blood, or an induced pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic cell population.

10. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells comprise CD34-positive cells.

11. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the hematopoietic stem cells comprise CD34-positive, CD38-negative, CD90-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD49f-positive, or combinations thereof cells.

12. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the hematopoietic progenitor cells comprise multipotent progenitors, common myeloid progenitors, common lymphoid progenitors, megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors, granulocyte-macrophage progenitors, lymphoid progenitors, erythroid progenitors, myeloid progenitors, or megakaryocytic progenitors.

13. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing is performed in serum-free medium.

14. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culture medium further comprises one or more cytokines, growth factors, small molecules, extracellular matrix components, or stromal-supportive factors.

15. The method of claim 14, wherein the one or more cytokines or growth factors are selected from stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, Flt3 ligand, interleukin-3, interleukin-6, interleukin-11, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, erythropoietin, angiopoietin-like proteins, insulin-like growth factor, or combinations thereof.

16. The method of claim 14, wherein the one or more small molecules comprise an aryl hydrocarbon receptor antagonist, UM171, SR1, a prostaglandin pathway modulator, a Wnt pathway modulator, a Notch pathway modulator, a TGF-beta pathway inhibitor, a ROCK inhibitor, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor, a pyrimidoindole derivative, or combinations thereof.

17. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing increases the number of CD34-positive cells relative to an input population.

18. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing increases the number or frequency of cells having long-term repopulating activity relative to a comparable culture lacking dermatopontin or the functional fragment thereof.

19. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing maintains or increases multilineage engraftment potential of the hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.

20. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing is performed for about 1 day to about 35 days.

21. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the culturing is performed under normoxic, hypoxic, or physiological oxygen conditions.

22. The method of any preceding claim, further comprising isolating, enriching, selecting, washing, formulating, cryopreserving, thawing, genetically modifying, transducing, electroporating, editing, differentiating, or administering the cultured hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.

23. The method of claim 22, wherein the genetically modifying comprises introducing a transgene, silencing construct, chimeric antigen receptor, T-cell receptor, gene-correcting construct, nuclease, base editor, prime editor, CRISPR-associated protein, zinc finger nuclease, TALEN, or recombinase.

24. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the cultured cells are formulated for transplantation into a subject.

25. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the subject is a human subject.

---

### 2. Composition Claims

26. **An ex vivo hematopoietic stem or progenitor cell culture composition,** comprising:  
   (a) a population of cells comprising hematopoietic stem cells, hematopoietic progenitor cells, or both; and  
   (b) dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof.

27. The composition of claim 26, further comprising a serum-free basal medium.

28. The composition of claim 26 or 27, further comprising one or more cytokines selected from stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, Flt3 ligand, interleukin-3, interleukin-6, interleukin-11, or combinations thereof.

29. The composition of any of claims 26-28, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is immobilized on a solid support.

30. The composition of any of claims 26-29, wherein the hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells are human CD34-positive cells.

31. The composition of any of claims 26-30, wherein the composition is substantially free of stromal cells.

32. The composition of any of claims 26-31, wherein the composition is substantially free of serum.

33. The composition of any of claims 26-32, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is present in an amount effective to maintain or increase hematopoietic stem cell self-renewal, viability, engraftment capacity, or multilineage differentiation potential.

---

### 3. Media and Kit Claims

34. **A culture medium for ex vivo culture of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells,** comprising dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof, and one or more hematopoietic stem cell-supportive cytokines.

35. The culture medium of claim 34, wherein the one or more hematopoietic stem cell-supportive cytokines comprise stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, and Flt3 ligand.

36. The culture medium of claim 34 or 35, wherein the medium is serum-free.

37. The culture medium of any of claims 34-36, further comprising albumin, insulin, transferrin, selenium, lipids, cholesterol, amino acids, vitamins, antioxidants, or combinations thereof.

38. **A kit for ex vivo expansion, maintenance, or preservation of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells,** the kit comprising dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof, and instructions for culturing hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells in the presence of said dermatopontin or functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof.

39. The kit of claim 38, further comprising one or more cytokines, basal media, culture vessels, coated culture surfaces, beads, scaffolds, hydrogels, transduction reagents, cryopreservation reagents, or cell selection reagents.

40. The kit of claim 38 or 39, wherein the dermatopontin or functional fragment thereof is provided as a lyophilized reagent, solution, coating reagent, immobilized substrate, or pre-coated culture vessel.

---

### 4. Product-by-Process and Therapeutic Use Claims

41. **A population of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells produced by the method of any of claims 1-25.**

42. The population of claim 41, wherein the population has increased engraftment potential, increased multilineage repopulating activity, increased CD34-positive cell number, increased primitive hematopoietic stem cell frequency, or increased colony-forming activity relative to a comparable population cultured in the absence of dermatopontin or a functional fragment thereof.

43. **A pharmaceutical composition** comprising the population of claim 41 or 42 and a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier, diluent, excipient, cryoprotectant, infusion medium, or buffer.

44. **A method of hematopoietic reconstitution in a subject,** comprising administering to the subject an effective amount of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells cultured ex vivo in the presence of dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof.

45. The method of claim 44, wherein the subject has received myeloablative conditioning, non-myeloablative conditioning, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, or gene therapy.

46. The method of claim 44 or 45, wherein the subject has a hematologic malignancy, bone marrow failure syndrome, immunodeficiency, hemoglobinopathy, metabolic disorder, autoimmune disease, or genetic hematopoietic disorder.

47. **Use of dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof for ex vivo expansion, maintenance, enrichment, or preservation of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.**

48. **Use of dermatopontin or a functional fragment, variant, derivative, fusion protein, or mimetic thereof in the manufacture of a culture medium, culture substrate, kit, or cell therapy product for ex vivo expansion, maintenance, enrichment, or preservation of hematopoietic stem cells or hematopoietic progenitor cells.**

---

## Exemplary Specification Language

In certain embodiments, the disclosure provides methods and compositions for ex vivo culture of hematopoietic stem cells and/or hematopoietic progenitor cells using dermatopontin, also referred to herein as DPT, or functional fragments, variants, derivatives, fusion proteins, conjugates, immobilized forms, or mimetics thereof. Without being bound by theory, DPT may provide one or more extracellular matrix-like, adhesion-modulating, survival-promoting, self-renewal-supporting, or niche-mimetic signals that support hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells during ex vivo culture.

As used herein, “hematopoietic stem or progenitor cells” or “HSPCs” include hematopoietic stem cells, long-term hematopoietic stem cells, short-term hematopoietic stem cells, multipotent progenitor cells, lineage-restricted progenitor cells, myeloid progenitor cells, lymphoid progenitor cells, erythroid progenitor cells, megakaryocytic progenitor cells, and mixed populations containing one or more of the foregoing. In some embodiments, the HSPCs comprise CD34-positive cells. In further embodiments, the HSPCs comprise cells expressing one or more markers selected from CD34, CD90, CD133, CD49f, CD117, CD45, and combinations thereof, and/or lacking or having reduced expression of one or more differentiation markers including CD38, CD45RA, CD14, CD15, CD19, CD3, CD41, CD71, or lineage markers.

The term “dermatopontin” includes naturally occurring DPT proteins from any species, including human, non-human primate, murine, rat, bovine, porcine, equine, canine, feline, or other mammalian DPT proteins, as well as recombinant, synthetic, purified, isolated, modified, tagged, conjugated, truncated, or engineered DPT polypeptides. In certain embodiments, the DPT comprises human DPT. In certain embodiments, the DPT comprises an amino acid sequence having at least about 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90%, 95%, 97%, 98%, or 99% identity to a naturally occurring DPT sequence while retaining HSPC-supportive activity.

A “functional fragment” of DPT refers to any portion of DPT that retains at least one activity of full-length DPT in an HSPC culture system, including, without limitation, the ability to increase HSPC survival, proliferation, expansion, adhesion, retention of primitive markers, colony-forming activity, multilineage differentiation potential, engraftment potential, self-renewal, or long-term repopulating activity relative to a control culture lacking the fragment. Functional fragments may include contiguous or non-contiguous portions of DPT, peptides derived from DPT, fragments fused to heterologous polypeptides, fragments immobilized on a substrate, or fragments chemically modified to improve stability, solubility, binding, or culture performance.

In some embodiments, DPT or a functional fragment thereof is provided in soluble form in a culture medium. In other embodiments, DPT or a functional fragment thereof is immobilized, adsorbed, covalently attached, crosslinked, incorporated, encapsulated, or otherwise associated with a culture surface, bead, membrane, fiber, hydrogel, scaffold, extracellular matrix preparation, microcarrier, nanoparticle, or culture vessel. In certain embodiments, DPT is used as a coating for culture vessels or microcarriers. In certain embodiments, DPT is used together with one or more matrix components, including fibronectin, collagen, laminin, vitronectin, tenascin, hyaluronic acid, heparan sulfate, proteoglycans, or fragments thereof.

The culture medium may be any medium suitable for ex vivo culture of HSPCs, including serum-containing, serum-free, xeno-free, chemically defined, or GMP-compatible media. The medium may comprise one or more cytokines or growth factors, including stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, Flt3 ligand, interleukin-3, interleukin-6, interleukin-11, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, erythropoietin, angiopoietin-like proteins, insulin-like growth factor, or combinations thereof. The medium may further comprise one or more small molecules that enhance HSPC expansion or maintenance, including aryl hydrocarbon receptor antagonists, UM171, SR1, prostaglandin pathway modulators, Wnt modulators, Notch modulators, TGF-beta pathway inhibitors, ROCK inhibitors, epigenetic modulators, or combinations thereof.

In certain embodiments, HSPCs are cultured in the presence of DPT or a functional fragment thereof for a period sufficient to expand, maintain, preserve, or enrich the HSPCs. Suitable culture periods include about 6 hours to about 60 days, about 1 day to about 35 days, about 2 days to about 21 days, about 3 days to about 14 days, or about 5 days to about 10 days. Culture may be performed under normoxic, hypoxic, or physiological oxygen conditions, including about 1% to about 21% oxygen.

In certain embodiments, DPT or a functional fragment thereof is present at a concentration effective to support HSPC culture. Exemplary soluble concentrations include about 0.001 ng/mL to about 10 mg/mL, about 0.01 ng/mL to about 1 mg/mL, about 0.1 ng/mL to about 100 µg/mL, or about 1 ng/mL to about 50 µg/mL. Where immobilized, DPT or a functional fragment thereof may be provided at a surface density effective to support HSPC adhesion, survival, expansion, or maintenance.

The methods may further comprise isolating HSPCs prior to culture, including by positive or negative selection using markers such as CD34, CD133, CD90, CD45RA, CD38, lineage markers, or combinations thereof. The methods may further comprise genetic modification of the HSPCs before, during, or after culture, including viral transduction, non-viral transfection, electroporation, genome editing, base editing, prime editing, transposon-mediated integration, mRNA delivery, protein delivery, or oligonucleotide delivery. The DPT-containing culture system may be used to preserve HSPC functionality during such manipulation.

In certain embodiments, HSPCs cultured with DPT or a functional fragment thereof are administered to a subject in need of hematopoietic reconstitution, immune reconstitution, gene-corrected cell therapy, or hematopoietic cell transplantation. The cells may be autologous, allogeneic, syngeneic, haploidentical, HLA-matched, or HLA-mismatched. The cells may be derived from cord blood, bone marrow, mobilized peripheral blood, placental blood, fetal liver, peripheral blood, embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells, or other hematopoietic sources.

In certain embodiments, ex vivo culture in the presence of DPT or a functional fragment thereof results in one or more improvements relative to culture without DPT or the fragment, including increased total nucleated cell number, increased CD34-positive cell number, increased frequency of primitive HSPCs, increased colony-forming units, increased multilineage differentiation, increased long-term culture-initiating cells, increased engraftment in an immunodeficient animal model, improved homing, improved viability, reduced apoptosis, reduced differentiation, or improved recovery following cryopreservation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention summary paragraph for a biotech patent covering DPT-containing cell culture media and kits for maintaining hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.
counterfactuals.output: The invention provides compositions and kits for the ex vivo maintenance, expansion, or culture of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), wherein the culture medium comprises an effective amount of DPT, optionally in combination with one or more basal media components, nutrients, serum substitutes, cytokines, growth factors, small molecules, antibiotics, or buffering agents. In certain embodiments, the DPT-containing medium supports survival, preserves stem/progenitor phenotype, maintains or enhances colony-forming capacity, reduces differentiation, and/or improves engraftment potential of HSPCs during culture relative to corresponding media lacking DPT. The invention further includes methods of culturing HSPCs by contacting a population of cells, including CD34+ cells, cord blood-derived cells, mobilized peripheral blood cells, bone marrow-derived cells, or induced pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic cells, with the DPT-containing medium under conditions sufficient to maintain or expand the cells. Kits of the invention may comprise DPT in liquid or lyophilized form, a basal culture medium or medium supplement, instructions for use, and optionally one or more cytokines such as stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, FLT3 ligand, interleukins, or other agents suitable for HSPC culture, thereby enabling standardized preparation and use of DPT-containing media for research, therapeutic manufacturing, transplantation, gene-modified cell production, or related applications.
